rationale.conceptual: The computational method is LDA-PBE DFT, a textbook approach. Building the initial double-perovskite structure with an organic cation requires some domain knowledge, but no novel algorithms or derivations are involved; it is a standard method with a minor variation (hybrid perovskite).
rationale.execution: The reproduction pipeline spans multiple stages: structure building, geometry optimization, band structure, optical property extraction for one compound, and formation energy calculations (including reference atom runs). This involves ~5 sequential, interdependent DFT runs with careful handoff of optimized geometries and k-point setup, typical of a non-trivial multi-stage computational workflow.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper uses standard DFT (LDA-PBE, plane-wave pseudopotentials) to compute electronic and optical properties of hybrid double perovskites. The method is well-established and the task reduces to setting up and running a known workflow, though the organic cation and double-perovskite ordering add minor structural complexity. Execution involves a multi-stage QE pipeline with structure construction, optimizations, band structures, optical calculations, and formation energies, which is non-trivial but standard for materials modeling. Resource needs are modest CPU-only, on the order of a few GB memory and negligible data volume.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The DFT calculations use modest plane-wave cutoffs (30/180 Ry) and a 4x4x4 k-point mesh for ~10-atom unit cells, with no GPU acceleration needed. Memory scales as a few GB for wavefunction storage; pseudopotential files are small (a few MB).
